correctness.rationale: Connected support at fixed edge count has j doubled right vertices and a nonempty incidence at every other right vertex; one doubled vertex suffices to join the two left vertices. The Walsh local factor is a_i b_i for a double and a_i+b_i for a single. Thus all d discordant positions must be doubled. Pulling out the discordant factors −1 and the product of all concordant signs leaves the elementary symmetric sum of order j−d of the concordant signs, i.e. K_{j−d}(h;n−d), with 2^{n−j} from the singles. Counting frequencies gives the stated rank and singular values with counting-measure convolution: d=j attains the least positive magnitude and the trivial character the largest. The case j=n has no forced zeros and consists of one graph; j<n admits d=j+1. At j=2 the d=1 root requires odd n, while d=0 has roots (n±√n)/2 iff n is square, since 2K₂=(n−2h)²−n. These are disjoint frequency classes, and the two roots for a square n≥4 are both valid. Ran independently written /workspace/branches/reproduce_fixed_excess.py with python3, checking all signed coefficients for (n,j)=(2,2),(3,2),(4,2),(4,3),(4,4),(9,2). The odd-square case had 168 zeros at d=0, 1260 at d=1 and rank 22124. The frozen reproducibility instructions name checks/check_unicyclic.py, but the packaged file is checks/check_bicyclic.py; inspection shows it in fact checks the unicyclic formula along with all fixed-excess signed spectra in its finite range. This path error does not invalidate the theorem.
